[i]A direct order from the Supreme Leader? Are you sure?

I have a hand-written letter right here. Bakr pulls out a letter from inside his coat and holds it out. Dawud takes the letter from his hand and tears it open, revealing a small paper within. His eyes dart over its contents before he lets it fall away from his hands and onto his table.

God why now? Surely we could have waited for some sort of instigation? Even framed a hostile act on their part? He brushed a hand through his hair.

We will have to do what he wills. It is rare for him to directly push through such legislation but alas. We should prepare for the economic shortcomings this will have for us. No doubt some others in the international community will not take kindly to this either.

Dawud shook his head. He slouched further into his chair as he pondered the order. Bakr sighed as he looked at his President's despair.

Ill finalise the contents of the act and have it passed in the next session of the Assembly.

Dawud did not even care to acknowledge Bakr as he bowed and walked out of the room.



By order of the President, I have called for this session of the Assembly to be convened. Only two members of this assembly are absent today which means we may comfortably move forward with today's session. I request that the member for Al-Khusumah, Bakr Mansuri, take the floor.

Bakr smoothened his clothing, a habit of his, as he got up from his bench and made his way to the table in the middle of the room. The room itself was in the shape of a semi-circle, with all the members of the Assembly sitting at benches and tables that arced through the room. There was a separate row for the bench of the members of the cabinet.

[b]The Mizrahel Sanctions Act[/b]

Thank you.

I have, by order of the Supreme Leader and President, drafted a comprehensive sanctions act targeting Mizrahel. Many of Mizrahels exports, named within this draft, will be completely embargoed by the Islamic Republic of Dabiristan. Other remaining exports will be subject to massive tariffs that will almost entirely make their imports into Dabiristan, unviable. Beyond trade, other financial actions will be implemented against Mizrahel, including but not limited to, the seizure of Mizraheli state assets and restrictions on currency exchange. Diplomatically, Dabiristan will recall any officials within Mizrahel whilst any Mizraheli officials within Dabiristan will be expelled. Mizrahel will also face visa bans, closure of land-crossings, restrictions on Mizraheli nationals working or studying within Dabiristan, and inspection or seizure of Mizraheli vehicles, ships, or aircraft entering national territory.

As Bakr finished his short introduction to the act, murmurs arose amongst the members of the Assembly. Bakr could clearly make out some of the conversations; perhaps the largest concern was the threat to Dabiristans own economy. He spoke again quickly.

For those concerned about our own economy, we are working rapidly towards bills that will help mitigate negative effects on our economy. We expect to have the most important bills ready by the next session.

Although the assembly was clearly opposed to the act, the knowledge that the Supreme leader himself had ordered this was enough to get most of the opposition parties in line. The ruling partys support of the act was already granted regardless. Following a short debate period, the bill was passed as the President declared the act as urgent By law, any proposal that was declared urgent would have to forgo a proper debate period and be voted on within the same session of assembly it was introduced in. 

The Act passed not because it was the will of the government, but because it had been ordered. That alone was sufficient. The Supreme Leader did not attend, did not speak, and did not need to.

Mizrahel would learn of the sanctions within the hour.[/i]

[b][u]Announcement From the Ministry of Foreign Affairs[/u][/b]

The government of President Fereydun Khan of Dhornaper applauds the announcements from Dabiristan and Irocco. Dhornaper reiterates its stance of non-recognition of Mizrahel. Mizrahel is a long-standing colonial state with an Elseyrian Jewish settler majority. Dhornaper does recognise Mizraheli claims to Shamat and will not accept it under current cirumstances.

Dhornaper similarly reiterates that it will maintain no direct trade with Mizrahel and confirms that its long-standing historical embargo of all Mizraheli goods will remain in place. Dhornaper is committed to its anti-colonial stance and prefers a diplomatic resolution to the Mizrahel situation with the ultimate goal of expulsion of Elseryian Jews and the equal treatment of indigenous Shamatine peoples in exchange for diplomatic recognition and an end to the embargo.

[spoiler=[b]THE FIRST ADVANCE - SEPTEMBER 16TH, 1953[/b]]

In a small village, a royalist unit sits in the fortifications they have constructed since the civil war began. The King ordered them to entrench and hold their position, apparently they lost a lot of equipment with the majority of the army going against him, yet they were one of the few to keep their entirety of their equipment, armored too. As a soldier shelters from the sun beneath the shadow his Lavian IST-32 (IRL the AMC.35), staring out into the desert landscape as he sipped on one of his remaining tea rations, he spots a dust plume on the horizon. At first he simply dismissed it as a local store owner returning from buying goods, but the dust plume gets too big for it to be a single vehicle. Taking out his binoculars, he stares back into the plume, as it trails behind something big. Getting closer, its shroud is broken, revealing a group of tanks being followed by a mass of men. Getting on his radio, he warns the others.

The town erupts in an uproar of movement, soldiers clambering into the amalgamation of different tanks they have been assigned. Old Llyndorran and Lavian tanks roll up to their positions, infantry holding inside houses and dug in positions, all watching, waiting. Then, the sound of aircraft ripped through the tension, a pair of planes appearing from behind the dust, cutting high into the sky before slowly rolling over, descending as if an eagle spotting its prey. Their first pass unleashed the rockets hidden under their wings, sending the armor-piercing rods into positions, tanks, and houses alike. One finds its mark in a Llyndorran C-14 (IRL A13 Mk II), setting its ammo off and blowing its hatches open, the turret resting lopsided and mangled as fire consumes it. Many however smash through the walls of houses, thankfully sparing the lives of due to the lack of explosives, however a family is fatally injured as they shelter in their house, an infant dying before army medics could even rush to the scene. 

The royalist guns opened fire on the aircraft as infantry did their best to aim with their light machine guns, peppering the sky with lead as the aircraft circle around the village, assessing the damage they caused. Either due to the resistance put up by the infantry or thinking they did their part, the aircraft retreat back to where they came, and now the assault troops are in firing range. The defenders two artillery guns open up, lobbing shells towards the advancing unit as it advances across the feature-sparce desert. The explosives arc into the formation, some causing casualties, some burrowing harmlessly into the ground and showering the advancing tanks with dirt and sand. Finally, it is time for the tanks to trade fire. Lifting their guns, the royalist armor unleashes a barrage of shells, aiming for the socialist tanks in front. The guns are ineffective however, bouncing harmlessly off the armor of the advancing tanks as they fire a return volley back.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

It was Shahids first taste of combat. The cacophony of sound and dust made him disoriented, but the other soldiers behind him kept him moving. Open desert all around him made him feel exposed, but they just need to get to the town and then he can take cover. That's easier said than done however. A clang of metal on metal followed by a loud whistle rings out, and Shahid falls. Struggling to get back up, he looks to the left and freeses. There beside him lies the man who was in formation behind him, or what's left of him in the least. His torso is gone, leaving his body cut in half with the other half splattered across the landscape. Shahid is hoisted from the ground by his commanding officer, a 19 year old, the oldest person in their squad.  Stay behind the tanks! he shouts before leaving Shahid, rushing back to his spot in the advance. 

They are almost upon the village now, and their tanks are beginning to return fire. Each blast kicks up dust, mixing with the exhaust fumes they already have to deal with from hugging the rear of the armor. The heavy tanks, built for this exact purpose, are loaded with mostly explosive shells, meaning that they have limited ability to deal with the enemy tanks taking shots at them until they can overwhelm them, but the limited shells they do have get put to work. While Shahid couldnt see it, the armor disabled the mobility of one of the royalist tanks, causing it to become a stationary emplacement, which was knocked out shortly after the first hit. 

Finally, they reached the town, and it was as if hell had come to earth. He rushed from behind the tank in front of him into a half-collapsed house, shaking as he leaned up against the wall, clutching his rifle. He dove for the floor as a machinegun raked the front of the house, splintering the door just inches from him. A group of other soldiers rush into the same house, taking cover next to him. Theres a machinegun up the street! Stay down! The soldier next to him nodded and repeated the same thing to another, apparently his squad lead. Okay! the sergeant yelled over the gunfire, You two come with me, he said, gesturing to two of the men who came in, You and this kid here I want to give us covering fire, then run across to the house on the other 
side and well flank it! 

Without saying another word, the three men bust through what is left of the door and begin rushing as fast as they can across the street. Managing to overcome his immense fear, Shahid rests his rifle on a windowsill and opens fire on the MG crew, and so does the other soldier. The crew takes cover before opening back up, narrowly missing both him and those running across the street. Now, seeing the others across the street, he takes his turn. As he runs, a bullet hits him, ripping into his upper arm. He makes it to the other side of the street, with the others already hailing a medic. The medic rushes over, applying sulfa powder and dressing the wound, as the others move on to flank the machinegun crew. Shahids part of the battle was now over, him being moved to a makeshift hospital established in a house, with fighting lasting into the late evening until the royalist troops finally retreated.[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]WAR OVERVIEW[/b]]

[b]THE SOCIALISTS FOCUS ON THE ROYALISTS - SEPTEMBER 1953[/b]

On September 15th, the Sabrati Socialist Revolutionaries launched an all out advance on the lands held by the Royalists. Moving in from the south, Revolutionary units advanced quickly through the royalist territory before being stopped at the Verta river, where royalist troops manage to hold the revolutionaries in a stalemate for now. Supplies are flowing in from the small border between the revolutionaries and Dhornaper, partially from the remaining royals in Nordheim. While Hydronian bombing raids did hamper the abilities of the revolutionary industrial base, it didnt stop them from using the supplies to produce guns, vehicles, and ammo to supply their advance. 

Up north, skirmishes turned into small battles as revolutionary units attempted to keep the coalition from looking south and potentially helping the royalists. The coalition still focused on attempting to negotiate with the royalists, their aid from Nordiheim being focused on equipping their few already trained troops with better equipment, and training new units. Royalists now focused their full might on holding at the river, buying whatever weapons they could acquire on the international market by selling off their gold reserves. It remains to be seen if anything will happen on the northern front between the Democratic coalition and the socialists, or if the socialists will wipe out the royalists before the coalition stops infighting long enough to form a military plan.[/spoiler]
